heat_treatment: solution-treated (980 C / 1 h, argon, air cool) - set 1
notes: Source states that 'the sample orientation with respect to the build plate starts at horizontal (0 deg) increasing to vertical (90 deg)', so printed 0 deg = horizontal = PERPENDICULAR to BD (= model 90 deg) and printed 90 deg = vertical = parallel to BD (= model 0 deg). Conversion applied. The per-orientation elongation values (0.20 / 0.25 / 0.30 at printed 0 / 45 / 90) are the project's existing blind-set figure read of Fig 15c; they agree with the source's explicit statement that elongation increases monotonically with build angle ('the lowest elongation at break should then be observed for the 0 deg specimens and increase gradually to a maximum for the 90 deg specimens') and with the Table 8 orientation average of 26 +/- 6% (mean of the three adopted values = 25%). UTS: the source tabulates only the orientation-AVERAGED value (Table 8: 970 +/- 74 MPa) and reports no significant UTS variation with build angle (only YS is reported to vary). The same 970 MPa is therefore assigned to all three orientations; the earlier in-repo blind script's per-orientation 990/970/950 MPa values were NOT re-used, because asserting an untabulated trend on a +/-74 MPa scatter is not defensible. Specimens have as-built surface finish (non-machined). Set 1 is solution-treated, NOT as-built; the as-built (un-heat-treated) condition is not reported by this source. Sets 2 (aged: 1286 MPa / 5%) and 3 (HIP+aged: 1201 MPa / 9%) are outside the scope of this dataset (heat-treated, single orientation). Printed 0 deg (horizontal, perpendicular to BD).

source_citation: Watring, D.S.; Benzing, J.T.; Hrabe, N.; Spear, A.D. Effects of laser-energy density and build orientation on the structure-property relationships in as-built Inconel 718 manufactured by laser powder bed fusion. Additive Manufacturing 2020, 36, 101425. doi:10.1016/j.addma.2020.101425
notes: Source states that 'build orientation is reported with respect to the build plate', so printed 0 deg = PERPENDICULAR to BD (= model 90 deg) and printed 60 deg = 30 deg from BD (recorded as 30 deg, category 'other'). Values from Table 3 (mean (STDEV)). All specimens as-built / non-heat-treated; tested at a strain rate of 1e-3 s^-1 on ASTM E8-16a specimens, which satisfies the room-temperature quasi-static requirement of this dataset exactly. Build condition 1 (printed 0 deg, laser energy density 38 J/mm^3): total elongation 0.06 +/- 0.012, uniform elongation 0.05 +/- 0.007, UTS 774 +/- 22 MPa, YS 639 +/- 10 MPa. FLAGGED ANOMALY (retained, not hidden): 6.91% lack-of-fusion porosity (relative density 93.09%) leaves UTS ~28% below the other two conditions and elongation below the nominal IN718 band (0.10-0.30); the source states the pore structure dominates the mechanical response. This is a genuine process-window effect and is precisely what makes the point useful for leave-one-process CV; exclude it for nominal-property CV.
